title: Review of c49's thermals controls: Weak. The 1.5x-resolution run (seed 3: 58 persistent splits, generation 11, 23/54 dividing caps pass 3 sqrt(area)) and the T=2000 run (87 splits, ~22-25 caps) replicate, and the local cut kills every cap in its strip, but on seeds 3 and 4 the caps outside the strip also fall (to 0.70x and 0.59x by t=480, against 1.00x and 0.81x fed)
summary: The finding's world unchanged. 1.5x resolution (WORLD_P dx 2/3, 192^2, seed 3, T=600): 58 persistent splits, generation 11, 28 bodies at the end, divmove.py 23/54 dividing caps travel >= 3 sqrt(area) between their own birth and division (5/54 in long axes). Long run (seed 3, T=2000): 87 persistent splits, generation 7, 21.8 bodies on average and 25 at the end (sheet: a steady crowd of rising caps from t~400 to 2000), 22/35 dividing caps pass. Local cut (the author's cut.py, copied with world.py, seeds 3 and 4): caps inside the strip 4 -> 0 and 1 -> 0 by t=410 and none return to t=480 (fed: 3-5 and 0-4 inside); caps outside the strip in the cut arm 30 -> 28 -> 24 -> 24 -> 21 and 27 -> 24 -> 23 -> 20 -> 16 at t=400/410/420/440/480, in the fed arm 30 -> 30 -> 27 -> 24 -> 30 and 27 -> 25 -> 27 -> 27 -> 22. The cut images (cut_s3.png) show a dark, fuel-poor halo around the strip: with fuel held at 0 and diffusing fast (kY 2), the strip is a fuel sink for its neighbourhood.

observations.D: pack_res15_s3: 58 persistent splits, generation 11; pack_long_s3/lineage.png: 87 persistent splits, population steady at ~22-25 caps to T=2000

seeds_run.result: pass for resolution and long run; local cut kills the strip's caps but outside caps fall to 0.70x (fed 1.00x)
local cut: strip's cap dies; outside caps fall to 0.59x (fed 0.81x)

controls_run.E: cut_s3.json and cut_s4.json: cut arm against the fed twin branched at t=400 (cut.py)

verdicts.limitation: E is not supported as a local-ablation result: the strip is a fuel sink that also thins the caps around it, so the neighbours do not keep their supply (the rubric's local-ablation option needs them to); the global fuel fork of the parent claim remains the E evidence, and E holds by construction there (heat is made only by burning). A strip that blocks fuel transport without absorbing it (zero flux at its edges) would be the cleaner local cut. The 1.5x-resolution population is denser and its tracker counts differ from 128^2 (as the author says), but the behaviour holds. One fresh seed for resolution and long run, two for the cut.
